37 A cell is connected in series with an ammeter and a variable resistor. A voltmeter is used to
measure the p.d. across the variable resistor. The resistance of the variable resistor is varied,
and the p.d. and the current are recorded.
The graph shows the variation with current of the p.d. across the variable resistor.

hints: Notice the y-intercept is $1.6 \text{ V}$ at zero current and the line falls to about $0.4 \text{ V}$ at $60 \text{ mA}$ - this is terminal p.d. $V$ against current $I$.
Recall $V = E - Ir$ for the cell, so the $V$ against $I$ graph is a straight line of gradient $-r$.
Pick two easy grid points such as $0 \text{ mA}, 1.6 \text{ V}$ and $60 \text{ mA}, 0.4 \text{ V}$, convert $\text{mA}$ to $\text{A}$, then calculate $|\Delta V / \Delta I|$.
walkthrough: The voltmeter reads the terminal p.d. $V$ across the variable resistor, while the ammeter reads the series current $I$.
For a cell of e.m.f. $E$ and internal resistance $r$, $E = V + Ir$, so $V = E - Ir$.
Therefore a graph of $V$ against $I$ has intercept $E$ and gradient $-r$. From the graph, $E = 1.6 \text{ V}$.
Choose two clear points: $I_1 = 0$, $V_1 = 1.6 \text{ V}$ and $I_2 = 60 \text{ mA} = 0.060 \text{ A}$, $V_2 = 0.4 \text{ V}$.
Change in p.d. is $\Delta V = 0.4 - 1.6 = -1.2 \text{ V}$ and change in current is $\Delta I = 0.060 - 0 = 0.060 \text{ A}$.
Gradient $= \Delta V / \Delta I = -1.2 / 0.060 = -20$, so $r = 20 \, \Omega$ with unit check $\text{V A}^{-1} = \Omega$.

A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 1000. It comes from mixing $\text{mA}$ with $\text{A}$ or inverting $\Delta V/\Delta I$.

B.explanation: This is the $1.6 \text{ V}$ intercept, which is the e.m.f. $E$, not the internal resistance $r$.

C.explanation: The magnitude of the gradient $\Delta V/\Delta I$ is $1.2 \text{ V} / 0.060 \text{ A} = 20 \, \Omega$, which equals $r$.

D.explanation: This is about $1.6 \text{ V} / 0.070 \text{ A}$, the total resistance $R+r$ at one point, not the internal resistance alone.
